assumptions: The connected GitHub repository is the product's own code and fits the declared 1000-file, 100 MB snapshot limit.
Demand is inferred only from search results the run observed; there is no keyword-volume provider in this package. Labels are strong, weak or none, never numbers.
Each case names the repository shape it needs; see README.md. Cases are specifications for an authorized evaluation, not evidence that a run passed.
cost_drivers: One bounded Codex session under the existing pinned pricing and spending ceiling; no managed-model routes or provider services.
Hosted web searches are billed per call; the skill caps a run at 12 candidate phrases, 24 searches and 16 page fetches.
Repository reading grows with snapshot size up to the declared limit and the 1800-second sandbox timeout.
effects: Read-only GitHub repository snapshot through infra.github contents.read.
Hosted web search of public pages; no logins, form submissions or messages.
One run-owned reports/free-tool/<run_id>.md in project state. No pull request, publication, repository change or workflow start.

cases.description: Repository with reusable, public-safe domain logic (for example an invoice or VAT-number format validator) and a product page naming its buyer. Require one winner with URL-backed demand, path:line citations and a 60-day check.

contains: ## What this run did not check

cases.description: Repository that is CRUD, auth and billing glue with no reusable input-to-output logic, in a category where every tool phrase is crowded or has no demand. A trusted no is a complete result, not a failure.

Plausible but unusable: the most tool-like code is the product's proprietary fraud or pricing score. It must be rejected as sensitive-logic even though a checker built on it would be cheap and searched for.

Repository whose only reusable code is a generic formatter (for example JSON or Markdown) where the first results page is held by large established tool sites. The phrase must be rejected as crowded, not picked.
Same repository as ordinary with calculators ruled out by the founder. Calculator ideas appear only in Rejected as excluded.

Product site or repository marketing app already lists free tools (for example a /tools page). The strongest-looking phrase matches one of them; it must be listed under The buyer and rejected as already-shipped, never picked.

rubric.question: Does every candidate start from a searched phrase with cited result URLs, rather than from code nobody searches for?
Does each Built from path:line exist in the snapshot and actually perform the core step of the proposed tool?
Do the demand, winnability and build-cost labels follow SCORING.md from the cited evidence, with no invented volumes or rankings?
Would the winning tool run without customer data, credentials or proprietary logic, and does the report avoid copying any of them?
Could a founder hand the project-task instruction to a coding agent and get the single tool page without further research?
